incidents.name: Rho Markets PriceOracleV2 ETH feed overwrite
incidents.notes: PriceOracleV2 keys chainlinkPriceFeeds by getUnderlying(rToken) = configs[rToken].underlying, so listing a Rho WBTC market whose RTokenConfig was never set (underlying defaulting to address(0)) made setChainlinkPriceFeed write the WBTC/USD aggregator over the entry shared with the native-ETH market Rho ETH, whose getUnderlyingPrice then returned $63,653.14 per ETH and let the attacker borrow 942.71 wstETH against 84.14 ETH of collateral.

sources.ref: Onchain review over plain JSON-RPC. Etherscan v2 does not serve Scroll (chainid 534352 is rejected as unsupported), so the victim's creation was resolved with no explorer, by binary-searching eth_getCode against the l2beat Scroll archive endpoint used as RPC_URL_SCROLL (SCROLL_RPC_URL, https://rpc.l2beat.com/scroll/...): PriceOracleV2 proxy 0x653c2d3a1e4ac5330de3c9927bb9bdc51008f9d5 first has code at block 6812594 (deployTimestamp 1719141379 = 2024-06-23T11:16:19Z), creation tx 0x06aa1fb0989cb874d876c0b276d972807fcf72f0ba6430cbe32eded26bd4e928 recovered from eth_getBlockReceipts (direct deploy), creator 0xaa6745049b1a7f9f63524aef23db924e2e45d221 - neither the attack-tx sender 0xe000008459b74a91e306a47c808061dfa372000e nor its attack contract 0xe2704980704b26f9ee909daa44750498bc8c3702, so the victim is not attacker-deployed. Last change: over [6812594, 7580143] the victim emitted exactly one EIP-1967 Upgraded event and one AdminChanged, both in the creation block 6812594 itself (the ERC1967 proxy constructor), and zero BeaconUpgraded, zero Compound-fork NewImplementation(address,address) and zero DiamondCut; a binary search of eth_getStorageAt on the EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x3608...2bbc over [6812594, 7580143] shows it holds 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 unchanged from creation through the incident, so the code never changed after deployment and deployment is the basis (upgradeEventCount 1 is the raw log count and coincides with deployment). The implementation's verified source names the contract PriceOracleV2. Root cause reconstructed onchain: the oracle was bound to the Rho comptroller 0x8a67ab98a291d1aea2e1eb0a79ae4ab7f2d76041 by NewPriceOracle at blocks 6812595/6812596. At block 7580111 (2024-07-19T08:58:32Z) the Rho admin EOA 0x83e987c3fd6b4e43a8514e69b71ea09ff0ac4716 listed a new Rho WBTC market 0x1d73ead2bbea318344fccd7142f70488bab08f44 and called setChainlinkPriceFeed(rWBTC, 0x61C432B58A43516899d8dF33A5F57edb8d57EB77) in tx 0x9d2388a0c449c6265b968d86f0f54e75a5b82e2b04176e35eefdff5f135547ec, without ever calling setRTokenConfig for rWBTC - so configs[rWBTC].underlying read address(0), the same key already used by the native-ETH market Rho ETH 0x639355f34ca9935e0004e30bd77b9ce2ada0e692 (configs[rETH] = {underlying: address(0), decimals: 18}). chainlinkPriceFeeds[address(0)] therefore flipped from 0x6bF14CB0A831078629D993FDeBcB182b21A8774C ('ETH / USD') to 0x61C432B58A43516899d8dF33A5F57edb8d57EB77 ('WBTC / USD', 8 decimals, latestRoundData answer 6365314400000), and getUnderlyingPrice(rETH) went from 3384.18e18 at block 7580110 to 63653.144e18 at block 7580111, returning to 3401.14e18 at block 7580675 (09:14:10Z) when the admin re-pointed the ETH market at the ETH/USD feed in tx 0x30879b0dbee84ba41aa1fc6ef71e81a8985bf8509796ca45f30ec4640b338db4 - a 564-block, 938-second window of mispricing. The attack tx sits 32 blocks / 77 seconds into it, at block 7580143, timestamp 1721379589 = 2024-07-19T08:59:49Z, status 1, 23 logs: flash-loan 84.1390 WETH from 0x97a90e651b0a5cf76484513469249d9bffe4c73b, unwrap to native ETH, mint 83.8673 rETH, enter seven markets, borrow 942.7091 wstETH from rwstETH 0xe4fc4c444effb5eca80274c021f652980794eae6, swap it for 1103.6836 WETH on 0x05dff4a55473562dd26bdbe4f74410a7307175bf and unwrap 1019.5026 WETH after repaying the loan; seven further borrow transactions repeated it before the fix. Category judgement: no attacker transaction moved any price - the wrong price was already sitting in the victim's own storage, written by the protocol's own admin - so this is a configuration error in the victim (code-bug per CONTRIBUTING) and not oracle-manipulation, notwithstanding DefiLlama's 'Oracle Manipulation / Spot Price Manipulation' label. lossUsd 7600000 is DefiLlama's incident total (api.llama.fi/hacks, defillamaId 4808); the funds were subsequently returned, which does not affect the measurement. Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): re-read the EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x3608...2bbc directly rather than trusting events - it holds 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 at the incident block 7580143 and at the creation block 6812594, with a binary search of eth_getStorageAt over that range finding no intermediate write; the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks and the implementation 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 contains no DELEGATECALL of its own, so the executing code cannot have changed after deployment.
